The matching paper is The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents by Zhexi Feng, Ruiyi Zhang, Yongbo Yang, et al. [1] It argues that for coding agents, relevance-ranked passages are not enough because sufficiency belongs to the set of evidence: individually relevant passages can still miss one requirement needed for the agent’s next decision. [1]

Feng et al. formulate state-conditioned minimal sufficient evidence recovery: given the agent’s current state, recover a compact combination of evidence that supplies what the next decision still lacks. [1] Their MSS-Complement method treats retrieval as set construction rather than ranking, and on SERBench it recovers complete evidence sets more often than a Qwen3 embedding plus reranking baseline. [1] Related work makes a similar sufficiency point for agent memory selection rather than repository retrieval, arguing that rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. [6]
